text:
Alex: Heads-up — around 11:40 UTC eu-west had a rapid GPU capacity drop (2 racks) causing routing to shear to other regions. We saw elevated latencies and a couple of fallbacks hit. Creating thread for runbook and followups.
DevOps-Bot: Incident created: INC-2065 — severity 2. Auto-failover engaged to reserve pools, telemetry recorded.
Maya: Can we get a concise timeline + what exactly tripped? Evictions, NVLINK, firmware?
Alex: Timeline: 11:38 detection, 11:40 two racks reported hardware faults leading to node evictions, 11:43 auto-evacuation completed, 11:44 traffic shifted to ams + sfo, 11:52 steady-state. Artifacts uploaded to #inc-artefacts (logs, flamegraphs).
Jason: Evictions show NVLINK fabric errors and repeated PCI resets. Kube events snippet:
```
11:40:12 Warning Evicted pod/model-abc namespace=infer reason=NodeDown
11:40:13 Warning Node Unhealthy node/gpu-rack-12 reason=KernelError message="gpu hfi reset"
11:40:15 Normal PodEvicted pod/model-xyz namespace=infer reason=Evicted
```
Priya: Key issue: our routing circuit-breaker thresholds for eu-west are too permissive. When 2 racks drop we immediately route broadly which saturates thin pools in other regions. Need layered fallback.
Liam: Agreed. Suggest layered fallback: 1) try same-region reserve warm-pools, 2) if warm exhausted, route to nearest region with per-region outflow rate-limits, 3) finally global spill. Also consider pre-warm heuristics on health degradation.
Sara: Also propose a "soft-failover" path before inter-region shift: reduce per-tenant concurrency + downgrade to quantized model-variant to preserve capacity. That buys time and reduces cost impact vs full cross-region shift.
Maya: Quick cost question — if we keep bigger warm pools we'll pay more. Need estimate of warm:hot ratio and expected $$ delta.
Alex: Draft runbook updates we should add: 
- Add explicit circuit-breaker thresholds for node-failure counts and eviction rates.
- Insert a soft-failover step (concurrency reduction + model-variant downgrade) before any inter-region reroute.
- Automate pre-warm reserve pools when node-health degrades for >30s (10 min pre-warm window).
- Implement per-region outflow-rate limiter in smart routing.
- Add monitor/alert for NVLINK/kernel GPU fabric error spikes.
- Postmortem action: infra SRE to validate firmware/driver matrix across racks.
Jason: I'll prototype the outflow-rate limiter. Quick config sketch: 
```json
{
  "region": "eu-west",
  "outflow_limit": 1200,
  "window_s": 60,
  "soft_failover": true
}
```
Priya: We also need an explicit rollback path in the runbook in case downstream regions start flapping: 
- Pause routing changes, 
- Throttle inter-region outflow to X rps, 
- Route back to degraded region with strict per-tenant concurrency caps.
Alex: Action items (owners):
- Jason -> prototype and test limiter (EOD).
- Priya -> update runbook with soft-failover + rollback steps (tomorrow AM).
- Liam -> capacity plan + cost estimate for warm pool sizing (48h).
- Maya -> finance sync for temporary warm-pool credits (48h).
- Alex -> write the postmortem and coordinate hardware validation (72h).
DevOps-Bot: Actions recorded: INC-2065-A1 (limiter prototype) INC-2065-A2 (runbook update) INC-2065-A3 (capacity plan) INC-2065-A4 (finance sync) INC-2065-A5 (postmortem).
Sara: Small tweak: increase eviction-detection window from 30s to 45s to reduce flapping-induced churn during transient spikes.
Alex: :thumbsup: I'll merge runbook PR after Priya's update and a quick SRE review. Can we target a playbook PR by tomorrow noon?
Priya: Ack — will open PR and add links to the simulated NVLINK test harness and the canary traffic job so we can validate behaviour before merging.
